items.title: Make main-write-lock reentrancy async-context-aware (AsyncLocalStorage owner-token)
items.context: In packages/main/src/core/main-write-lock.ts: the bare process-global heldLockPaths Set (line 271) mis-classifies a CONCURRENT async sibling as a nested reentrant caller because it cannot distinguish synchronous nesting from async interleaving across an await. Introduce an AsyncLocalStorage-based owner context. Recommended design (a2): keep the on-disk acquisition + a process-global record of WHICH async-context-owner holds each lockKey, and change the reentrancy predicate in withReentrantMainWriteLock (line 304) AND acquireMainWriteLockRegistered (line ~352) from plain heldLockPaths.has(lockKey) to has(lockKey) && currentAlsContextOwnsIt. Outermost acquire runs fn (or the acquire/release window) inside als.run(ownerToken, ...) so genuine synchronous nesting (DONE->audit) inherits the same ALS context and still passes through, while a concurrent INIT_CHECK in a separate ALS context correctly contends on the on-disk mkdir lock (and fail-fasts / waits per options) instead of skipping acquisition. The acquire/release-pair form used by the DONE merge in transition-orchestrator.ts must establish the ALS context around its critical section; make the minimal change there to wrap the DONE main-merge window. Update isMainWriteLockHeldInProcess test helper accordingly. The on-disk mkdir mutex behavior is UNCHANGED.

items.title: Fix global-fallback guard brand mismatch in codex-adapter-checks.ts
items.context: In packages/main/src/core/codex-adapter-checks.ts:644 the globalCoreCandidates array only lists { @lattice-agent/core }. The actual installed global npm link is @koala-agent/core, so checkGlobalFallback never finds the global core and never emits its intended heartbeat-only warning. Add a second candidate { path: join(globalRoot, @koala-agent, core), label: @koala-agent/core } so the guard fires for the real install and the operator sees the correct signal that the global lattice resolves to main dist (heartbeat-only, not current-worktree evidence). ~2-3 lines. Do NOT change any other guard logic.

items.title: Extend main-write-lock self-smoke + CHANGELOG
items.context: Add a DETERMINISTIC async-interleave negative case to the main-write-lock coverage smoke (packages/main/src/tasks/main-write-lock-coverage.ts or the dedicated lock smoke): orchestrate two async operations so operation A acquires the lock and parks at a controllable await; inside that await window, operation B (separate ALS context) attempts acquire and MUST NOT be mis-classified as reentrant pass-through (it should contend / fail-fast). Also assert genuine synchronous nesting still passes through (no regression to self-deadlock). CHANGELOG Unreleased entry under Test infrastructure documenting the reentrancy-race fix + the guard brand fix. Verify: npm run test:all green; the lock-coverage smoke passes incl the new case.
